{{Quote|Most of the best freighter pilots can be found here. Only watch your step. This place can be a little rough.|Obi-Wan Kenobi, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
'''Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina''', also known as '''Chalmun's''', '''Chalmun's Cantina''', '''double-c'''/'''ceecee''' by the city militia, the '''Mos Eisley Cantina''' or simply '''The Cantina''', was a popular [[Cantina/Legends|drinking and dining establishment]] located in the city of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] on the desert [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].

==History==
===Early history===
[[File:MScantina_schematics.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Mos Eisley cantina schematics]]
The single-story building was constructed by [[Cedo Partu]], an early pioneer and Mos Eisley town leader, as a fortification against [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]],<ref name="Refresher 91" /> and stood as one of the original spaceport's oldest blockhouses until its conversion.<ref name="ANH novel">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref> Changing ownership over the years, the building saw use as an armory, a brewery, and a flophouse for vagrants. Before the inception of the cantina, the site was occupied by [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr Monks]] and the [[Vriichon brothers/Legends|Vriichon brothers]], who, before the purchase by [[Chalmun/Legends|Chalmun]], were running an illegal [[Spice/Legends|spice]] den on the site and burying bodies in the basement.<ref name="ITWSWT">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref>

Identified only by a sign over the door reading simply "Cantina," the cantina was a popular gathering place for [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] and [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], and the center of a host of criminal activity in the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] of Mos Eisley, Tatooine. It was run by the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] Chalmun, who purchased the building using gambling profits earned on [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]].<ref name="GG7">''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]''</ref>

===Clone Wars===
When the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] erupted between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], Tatooine remained neutral as it was not a member of either institution. However, as the war approached its conclusion, the Confederacy made an [[Invasion of Tatooine|attempt]] on Mos Eisley. The Republic troops made it to the city first, and the elite [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] [[X1]] and [[X2]] took over the cantina and used it as a staging area from which to defend the center of the city. [[Jedi General/Legends|General]] [[Ferroda]], a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]], managed to take the city, and the troops left the cantina intact.<ref name="SWBES">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron]]''</ref>

===Galactic Civil War===
{{Quote|The cantina? Well, it's not really dangerous. There hasn't been an incident in the cantina for some time. A Rodian bounty hunter was shot there by one of his associates, and an Aqualish lost his arm in a barfight the same day. But since then it's been pretty quiet. Wuher likes to run a quiet cantina.|Mayor Mikdanyell Guh'rantt, to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:MMG">{{SWGcite|exp=RotW|type=conversation|Mayor Mikdanyell Guh'rantt|Tatooine}}</ref>}}
Nearly two decades later, the cantina was still profiting under the stewardship of Chalmun, bringing in profits even under the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The [[Droid/Legends|droid]]-hating [[Wuher/Legends|Wuher]] maintained the bar during the day, and the cheerful bar wench [[Ackmena/Legends|Ackmena]] tended the place at night. Bouncers such as [[Tork]] would regulate the rowdy crowd, tossing out those who shot other patrons.<ref name="ITWSWT" /> Other employees included [[Lurval]] and the [[Bartender/Legends|bartender]] [[Muna Skish]].<ref name="SWG:C">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Trader|Crafting|Tatooine}}</ref>

At one point a holographic video screen was installed by Chalmun for sports broadcasts, but it was removed after the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] entertainment feeds faced constant interruptions from Imperial alerts.<ref name="Refresher 91" /> The cantina gained a permanent band when the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] [[Figrin D'an/Legends|Figrin D'an]] gambled away the ownership of the [[Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes/Legends|Modal Nodes]]' instruments in a rigged card game with [[Kardue'sai'Malloc/Legends|Kardue'sai'Malloc]].<ref name="Empire Blues">{{StoryCite|story=Empire Blues: The Devaronian's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> One reason Chalmun's Cantina was so popular among spacers was the [[Fabritech/Legends|Fabritech]] [[EPT-212|droid detector]] that Chalmun installed in the foyer.<ref name="Refresher 91" /> For a long time, [[Mark IV sentry droid/Legends|Imperial Sentry Droids]] made private discussions between smugglers and crime bosses all but impossible. While the detector didn't keep the Sentry Droids out, it did warn everyone that their activities and discussions were about to come under Imperial scrutiny. This enabled everyone time to compose themselves and present a perfectly innocent demeanor. Chalmun's also had a strict "No Droids" policy to prevent people from bringing their own droids into the Cantina with them.

[[File:MScantina_Luke.png|thumb|left|200px|Luke Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi in the cantina, meeting Chewbacca]]
Following the deaths of [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen]] and [[Beru Whitesun Lars/Legends|Beru Lars]], in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and the young [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] made their way to the cantina to look for a pilot to the [[Alderaan system/Legends|Alderaan system]]. There, they finally met with the pilot who would soon fly them to [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]]: [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and his copilot [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]]. During talks over a trip to Alderaan, Skywalker encountered the [[Aqualish/Legends|Aqualish]] scoundrel [[Ponda Baba/Legends|Ponda Baba]], who threatened to kill him. In defense of the young man, Master Kenobi [[Cho mai/Legends|removed]] Baba's arm with his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. When the Jedi and his charge quickly fled attention in the cantina, Han Solo prepared to leave but was stopped by the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]]. Greedo, employed by [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] to kill Solo in compensation of a debt the smuggler owed, managed to fire a single shot that missed before Solo killed him.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}: [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]]</ref>

After the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], [[Talon Karrde]] and [[Dravis]] supervised the operations of the [[Smugglers' Alliance|Smuggler Alliance]] from the back rooms of the Mos Eisley Cantina.<ref name="SWG:SA">{{SWGcite|exp=JtL|type=other|Smuggler Alliance}}</ref>

In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> the [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] [[Gendra]] recruited several [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]], including a [[Merchant/Legends|trader]] and an [[entertainer]], to help his friend Chalmun who was facing several problems at the cantina. The trader crafted new glassware and was eager to prepare [[Jerky/Legends|meat jerky]] and [[Spice tea/Legends|spiced tea]] for the customers of the cantina. The entertainer agreed with performing in the cantina, dancing and [[Musician/Legends|playing music]] for the patrons who where delighted by the shows.<ref name="SWG:C" /><ref name="SWG:E">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Entertainer|Entertainment|Tatooine}}</ref>

[[File:Ackmenas_patrons.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Ackmena, along with the rest of her patrons, in the Cantina]]
In 1 ABY, Tatooine, along with the rest of the [[Tatoo system/Legends|system]], was put under Imperial curfew by an [[Unidentified Moradmin Bast look-alike|Imperial Moff]]. [[Ackmena/Legends|Ackmena]], the bartender at the cantina at the time, received the message, and responded by singing "[[Goodnight, But Not Goodbye/Legends|Goodnight, But Not Goodbye]]" to her guests as she ushered them out the door.<ref name="Holiday Special">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref> During the curfew period, droids were also assigned to a waiting area if they accompanied patrons. At one point, a Jawa infected with [[Bledsoe's disease]], died shortly after drinking, which caused the bartender to initially think he drank himself to death until a patron revealed otherwise. Presumably, everyone in the cantina that day died from infection, save for Luke Skywalker and Anduvil, who managed to escape in time as soon as they witnessed the Jawa's death.<ref name="Sojourn">"[[Tatooine Sojourn]]"</ref>

Chalmun's Cantina was firebombed shortly after the death of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]],<ref name="The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook">''[[The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref> forcing a rebuilding. During the chaos surrounding Jabba's death, the Cantina was attacked again by a swoop gang led by [[Mossol]] the Menace, but the repair droids put out the fire. A group of spacers then helped Chalmun free his friend [[Rejeff]].<ref name="Passage from Perdition">{{WEGCite|story=The Passage From Perdition|book=Mos Eisley Adventure Set}}</ref>

A few years after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] and [[Mirax Terrik Horn|Mirax Terrik]] visited the cantina on their way to visit [[Huff Darklighter]]'s estate.  Corran remarked that the tables in the cantina had probably seen more combat then most of [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron's]] [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighter]]s.  Corran told Mirax that if he had been asked to plan a raid it would have started with strafing runs. 

It remained open five years after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], when Han Solo returned there to meet with the smuggler [[Dravis]] in an unsuccessful attempt to enlist him in cargo work for the New Republic.<ref name="Heir to the Empire">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref> The cantina was also open at least 15 years later, a man named [[Zekk]]&mdash;working as a bounty hunter&mdash;sought [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] to share with him information on [[Bornan Thul]].

==Layout==
{{Quote|You will never find a more wretched hive of scum and villainy.|Obi-Wan Kenobi, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Episode 4" />}}
[[File:ITW_Chalmuns_cantina.jpg|thumb|250px|Cantina cutaway]]
A single-story building made of sandstone, the cantina consisted of a bar area, private offices, a VIP lounge, a private [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]], a basement, and a phony shop in the rear. With a maximum occupancy of 102 humanoids, the facility catered to all sorts from across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], with spacious areas and wide arched doorways to allow patrons of all sizes passage.<ref name="ITWSWT" />

Entering through a small portal on one side of the building, a small passage curved around into the main bar area. The bar, featuring many themed spigots which resembled the head of an [[IG-series/Legends|IG-series]] [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]], was capable of producing several dozen drinks of Chalmun's concocting. Surrounded by eight different alcoves filled with stools, tables, and even a bandstand, the bar wrapped from the public area around into the more private back room. Outside of public view, several secret rooms existed to house sleeping areas for fugitives fleeing the law. At the very back of the building, an open-air hangar housed Chalmun's private shuttle, which could be used routinely to transport liquor, or for escape.<ref name="ITWSWT" />

Inside one of the building's domed portions, Chalmun kept his offices. Including his own private bar, the Wookiee's office space was home to his security chief and several confiscated weapons. The back rooms of the building ran parallel to the outside bazaar, which sold droid parts and scrap metal. Chalmun maintained a shop out back that sold clothes and other goods. Its domed roof sported a communications jammer disguised as a [[Moisture vaporator/Legends|vaporator]].<ref name="ITWSWT" />

Underneath the cantina, a small cellar had been built long before Chalmun came to Tatooine. The bartender, Wuher, used the basement to cook up new brews for his clients; previous owners had used it as a catacomb.<ref name="ITWSWT" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Voren_Cantina.png|thumb|right|250px|Concept art of the cantina]]

Filming for the cantina exteriors in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']] took place in [[Ajim]], Djerba, [[Tunisia]] on [[April 2]]&ndash;[[April 3|3]], [[1976]]. Most of the interior shots were from Stage 6 at [[Elstree Studios]] on [[April 13]]&ndash;[[April 21|21]].

Chalmun's Cantina was also in ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'', set months after ''A New Hope'', and shown during a night shift.

An [[IG-88 assassin droid/Legends|IG-88]] head can be seen behind the bartender when Ponda Baba's arm is cut off. A full one can also be seen in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] when Chewbacca is looking for [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]]&mdash;both are white, while earlier in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' an IG-88 bounty hunter is colored gray.

It is possible that the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|Episode I]] [[Podracer/Legends|podracer]] [[Gasgano/Legends|Gasgano]] was present around the time of Luke Skywalker's meeting with Han Solo. Although not seen in the movie, [[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] points out a "multifingered former podracer, now a deft pickpocket" who can be located inside the cantina. It may be another [[Xexto/Legends|Xexto]] podracer; however, the only officially named Xexto podracer is Gasgano.

The cantina was featured in an official [[1979]] drunk-driving PSA. In 2007, [[StarWars.com|the official site]] [http://www.starwars.com/episode-iv/bts/article/cantinapsa.html made it available].

A skit on a [[1977]] episode of [[Wikipedia:The Richard Pryor Show|''The Richard Pryor Show'']] took place in the "''Star Wars'' Bar," with Pryor playing the bartender. Though the skit did not reuse the original sets, many of the masks from ''A New Hope''{{'s}} cantina scene were used for the patrons.

The [https://www.rebelscum.com/photo.asp?image=/sote/soteTC023.jpg "It'th Greedo'th Uncle" card] from the [[1996 Topps Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' trading card set]] mistakenly refers to the Mos Eisley cantina as a "casino."
